paper.title_en: The Mass-Angular Momentum Inequality for Multiple Black Holes
paper.abstract_en: This is the second in a series of two papers to settle the conjectured mass-angular momentum inequality for multiple black holes. More precisely, we show that for a complete, simply connected, maximal initial data set for the Einstein equations with multiple ends that are either asymptotically flat or asymptotically cylindrical, the ADM mass of any asymptotically flat end admits a lower bound given by the square root of total angular momentum, under the assumption of nonnegative energy density and axisymmetry. Moreover, equality is achieved in this mass lower bound only for a constant time slice of an extreme Kerr spacetime. The proof is based on a novel flow of singular harmonic maps with hyperbolic plane target, under which the renormalized harmonic map energy is monotonically nonincreasing. Relevant properties of the flow are achieved through a refined asymptotic analysis of solutions to the harmonic map equations and their linearization.
